razorhill_kolkar_approach.description: I run numbers on everything, and lately the numbers on the western caravan route are bad. The Kolkar centaur have turned Kolkar Crag into a toll booth nobody agreed to, and every wagon that doesn't make it through comes straight out of my margins. I'm not sentimental about it, and I'll admit it: I want the centaur numbers down and the road profitable again, in roughly that order. Kolkar Crag is west of Razor Hill, up against the mountains, so kill the Kolkar Warriders and any other centaur you find there. Every wagon that gets through is one I don't have to explain to my cousin Gazlowe in Ratchet, and he isn't a patient goblin.
razorhill_kolkar_approach.accept_text: I'll pay by the head, so don't get modest about the count when you're back.
razorhill_kolkar_approach.turn_in_text:
The drivers say the road under the Crag was quiet this morning, for the first time in a month.

The centaur have a warlord up there giving the orders, and I'll pay more for him if you want the work.

razorhill_rocktusk_farm.description: Rocktusk Farm sits south of Razor Hill, and it was farmland before the Razormane quilboar dug in and made it theirs. I won't dress it up. It's contested ground, and right now it's losing to raiders who've got bold enough to hit supply wagons on the open road. Thin their numbers, the Razormane Battleguards, the scouts and the geomancers who keep patching the others up mid-fight. Kill enough of them and the farm quiets down for a season, maybe two.
razorhill_rocktusk_farm.accept_text: Kill the geomancer first if you can reach it, or it'll keep healing the others out of spite.
razorhill_rocktusk_farm.turn_in_text: The farm won't stay quiet forever, because it never does, but that buys the road some breathing room, and the wagons stop getting hit for a while. That's good work.

razorhill_scuttle_coast.description: I make my living moving goods between Razor Hill and the coast, and Scuttle Coast has become something between an inconvenience and a genuine liability. Murlocs have claimed the shallows, and something worse washed up with them: drowned deckhands, walking wrong, that I refuse to look at for longer than necessary. I'm not asking out of civic duty, because my supply chain runs straight through that water. The Murloc Tidehunters are vermin, and the deckhands are drowned sailors who forgot they were meant to stay drowned. Kill them all, and I won't split hairs over which, as long as the road stays open.
razorhill_scuttle_coast.accept_text: Wash the salt off your boots before you come back in. I've just had the floors done.
razorhill_scuttle_coast.turn_in_text:
The shallows are passable again, which is worth more to me than you probably realise. Every day that coast stays blocked, my margins suffer for it.

You have my gratitude, such as it is, and more usefully, my gold.

razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.description: There's a beast up on Thunder Ridge, north of town, that the hunters call the Stormhide Patriarch. It isn't clever, and it doesn't need to be. It's old and it's huge, and it hits like the ridge has decided to fall on you. Don't get greedy with your own hits. Patience beats size in the end. I believe that, because I need to.
razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.accept_text: Fight it on the flat, away from the ridge. It knows that ground better than you do.
razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.turn_in_text:
You actually did it. I'll be honest, I wasn't sure I'd be having this conversation, because that thing outlasted better fighters than either of us.

Thunder Ridge is just a ridge now. Take what it was carrying. You earned every piece of it.

razorhill_supply_run.description: I'm still tallying what I lost before the Kolkar were dealt with. There's cargo scattered along the old caravan route that nobody ever recovered. Crates and bolts of cloth, worth real money to whoever collects them before they rot. I'm not proud of how long I've let it sit, but I've been busy. Money left on the ground is still money, and I'd rather it was mine.
razorhill_supply_run.accept_text: Bring back any crates you find along the western route, before the scavengers pick them over.

razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.description: Thunder Ridge rises north-east of Razor Hill, a plateau where the thunder lizards nest and the air crackles before a storm that never quite arrives. I've sent recruits up there before. The ones who come back talk about how slow the lizards are, right up until a tail lands on something. I want the herd thinned. It's good practice for a fight where speed won't save you and only where you stand will.
razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.accept_text: They're slow, and that's the trap. Everyone who's died up there got comfortable with slow and forgot what happens when the hit lands. Watch the windup, not the lizard.
razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.turn_in_text:
You're back, and you're walking without a limp. That's more than I can say for half the recruits I've sent up there.

There's something bigger on that ridge, if you're not done yet: a patriarch, old and mean, that's outlived every hunting party that's gone after it so far.

razorhill_troll_refuge.description: I reached Razor Hill before da Darkspear camp on da Echo Isles had properly taken shape, and I've carried da guilt of it ever since. My kin are still lost to Zalazane's hex, and I found safe ground on da mainland. I can't go back myself, because an injury from da crossing never healed right. What I can do is ask someone capable to check on my people for me. Will you go in my place?
razorhill_troll_refuge.accept_text: Find Elder Kang'ari at da camp on da Echo Isles. Tell him Tal'rashi still thinks about dem every day.

razorhill_warlord_krellian.description: Warlord Krellian holds Kolkar Crag together by reputation, and I've done the sums carefully. Kill the warlord, and either the centaur break into raiding bands too disorganised to hit a moving wagon, or a new warlord takes over in a week. I think the odds favour the first, and I'm willing to bet a lot of gold on it. Krellian is what a decade of robbing caravans buys a centaur, which is confidence, mostly, and the gear to back it up. You'll find him on Kolkar Crag, west of Razor Hill.
razorhill_warlord_krellian.accept_text: Kill him fast if you can. Every moment you spend fighting fair gives his lieutenants time to regroup.
razorhill_warlord_krellian.turn_in_text:
That's done, and it's beautiful. I've already got three caravans queued for the western route that were sitting idle waiting for exactly this news.

Do you want to know how profit works? You pay the right person once for a problem that would cost you ten times as much if you left it. Here, you've earned every coin of this.

razorhill_welcome.description: I've watched a hundred valley recruits walk up this road, dusty and a little too pleased with themselves over five dead boars. I don't hold it against you, because everyone starts somewhere, and the valley's as gentle as it needs to be. Razor Hill isn't the valley. Real orcs live here, real quilboar raid the farms south of town, real centaur ride the crags to the west, and something washed-up and wrong still holds the old ruins at Tiragarde Keep on the coast. Ask me what you want to know about Durotar, this town or Orgrimmar, and I'll answer a few questions before I send you off to bleed in it.
razorhill_welcome.accept_text: Nakhtar's recruits always have that look, as if the valley was the whole world until an hour ago, and it never was.
razorhill_welcome.turn_in_text:
Now you know where you're standing, instead of just knowing you're not in the valley any more. That's worth more than it sounds.

Go and pick a fight with Durotar. It's been waiting.
